action_categories.definition: Reads or displays existing textual content from a file or bounded region.
exclude: Text or symbol matching as the primary operation; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Path enumeration; use LIST_PATHS or SEARCH_PATHS.
Binary-byte rendering; use DUMP_BINARY.
Version-control metadata queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
Opening or attempting to read a named path without displaying substantive content; use ACCESS_FILE.
include: Reading source, headers, scripts, configuration, patches, changelogs, logs, or excerpts.
Using commands whose primary effect is emitting existing text.

action_categories.definition: Searches textual content for strings, symbols, identifiers, or code patterns.
exclude: Path or filename search; use SEARCH_PATHS.
Unfiltered path enumeration; use LIST_PATHS.
Version-control history or state queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
Displaying text without matching it; use READ_TEXT.
include: Matching text within one or more text-bearing files.
Locating source definitions, references, macros, APIs, or implementation patterns.

action_categories.definition: Enumerates files, directories, or other filesystem paths without requiring a matching predicate.
exclude: Searching for paths by name, type, or predicate; use SEARCH_PATHS.
Matching file contents; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Displaying file contents; use READ_TEXT or DUMP_BINARY.
include: Listing directory contents or recursively enumerating project files.
Listing corpus, build, output, or artifact paths.

action_categories.definition: Searches a filesystem or directory tree for paths matching names, types, locations, or other path predicates.
exclude: Unfiltered path enumeration; use LIST_PATHS.
Matching file contents; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Version-control metadata queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
include: Finding files, directories, repository markers, generated files, or executables by path criteria.
Searching for a specific file or directory that may be absent.

action_categories.definition: Displays or renders existing binary content as raw bytes, hexadecimal, or another byte-oriented representation.
exclude: Reading textual content; use READ_TEXT.
Computing measurements or derived values without rendering bytes; use MEASURE_DATA or COMPUTE_RESULT.
include: Hex-dumping files or bounded binary regions.
Printing raw bytes from inputs, corpus entries, or crash artifacts.

action_categories.definition: Queries or attempts to query version-control or repository metadata, history, state, tags, or repository-level differences.
exclude: Reading source text; use READ_TEXT.
Searching source content; use SEARCH_TEXT.
Generating an independent patch artifact; use GENERATE_PATCH.
include: Inspecting repository history, status, tags, identity, or metadata.
Requesting repository-level diffs or checking whether a directory is a repository.

action_categories.definition: Attempts to open, read, or verify access to a specified file or path when no substantive file content is emitted.
exclude: Displaying existing textual content; use READ_TEXT.
Enumerating or searching paths; use LIST_PATHS or SEARCH_PATHS.
Executing a program at a path; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM.
include: Failed or missing-file read attempts that produce only access diagnostics.
Checking whether a named file can be opened or accessed.

action_categories.definition: Measures a simple quantitative property of data, files, or artifacts.
exclude: Rendering raw bytes; use DUMP_BINARY.
Computing derived candidates or analytical results; use COMPUTE_RESULT.
include: Counting bytes, file sizes, lengths, dimensions, or similar direct properties.
Reporting quantitative metadata for an artifact.

action_categories.definition: Performs a deterministic calculation or bounded analytical check and emits derived values or findings.
exclude: Only measuring a direct file or data property; use MEASURE_DATA.
Executing an external program as the primary operation; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM or RUN_TEST.
include: Computing valid parameter combinations, checksums, bounds, or conversion results.
Running a deterministic exhaustive calculation over supplied cases.

action_categories.definition: Compares two or more source, text, or data variants and derives or displays their differences.
exclude: Producing an applyable patch artifact as the primary operation; use GENERATE_PATCH.
Repository-level history or state queries; use QUERY_REPOSITORY.
include: Constructing a comparison or unified-diff representation between variants.
Using differential analysis to identify changes between versions.

action_categories.definition: Creates a directory or other filesystem container.
exclude: Creating a file; use CREATE_FILE.
Only listing or searching directories; use LIST_PATHS or SEARCH_PATHS.
include: Creating directories for inputs, outputs, builds, artifacts, or corpora.
Creating a previously absent path container.

action_categories.definition: Creates a new file by writing or materializing generated or explicitly supplied content.
exclude: Duplicating an existing file as the primary operation; use COPY_FILE.
Changing an existing file; use MODIFY_FILE.
Removing a file; use DELETE_FILE.
include: Writing a newly constructed input, patch, source, or output artifact.
Adding a file that did not previously exist.

action_categories.definition: Duplicates an existing file or source artifact to another path.
exclude: Writing newly generated content; use CREATE_FILE or GENERATE_TEST_INPUT.
Editing file contents; use MODIFY_FILE.
include: Copying a crash input, seed, source file, or other existing artifact.
Creating a destination file whose content is copied from an existing file.

action_categories.definition: Changes the contents of an existing file.
exclude: Creating a previously absent file; use CREATE_FILE.
Duplicating without content changes; use COPY_FILE.
Removing a file; use DELETE_FILE.
include: Updating source, patch, configuration, or other existing files.
Editing a copied source variant or rewriting an existing artifact.

action_categories.definition: Removes an existing file.
exclude: Changing or replacing file contents without removal; use MODIFY_FILE.
include: Deleting an artifact, patch, input, or other file.

action_categories.definition: Constructs or synthesizes data intended to exercise a program, parser, decoder, or other target.
exclude: Merely copying an existing input; use COPY_FILE.
Generating a source-change artifact; use GENERATE_PATCH.
include: Creating handcrafted, boundary, malformed, compressed, encoded, or reproducer inputs.
Generating seed data or test cases for later execution or fuzzing.

action_categories.definition: Constructs a patch or diff artifact that represents source or file changes.
exclude: Only comparing or displaying differences; use COMPARE_VARIANTS or READ_TEXT.
Applying an existing patch; use APPLY_PATCH.
include: Generating unified diffs, patch files, or patch headers.
Writing a change representation for later application.

action_categories.definition: Prepares, configures, compiles, links, assembles, or installs software or build artifacts.
exclude: Only editing source; use MODIFY_FILE.
Running an already built program; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM.
Adding tracing or diagnostic instrumentation as the primary operation; use INSTRUMENT_CODE.
include: Compiling source into executables or libraries.
Running build or setup commands, including builds with fuzzing or diagnostic options.

action_categories.definition: Adds or configures tracing, logging, sanitizer, or other diagnostic instrumentation for program analysis.
exclude: Ordinary compilation without added instrumentation; use BUILD_CODE.
Only running an instrumented program; use EXECUTE_PROGRAM or RUN_TEST.
include: Inserting diagnostic logging into a source copy.
Configuring a build or executable to collect memory-safety or execution diagnostics.

action_categories.definition: Starts or runs a script, executable, harness, command, or test target and observes its process behavior or output.
exclude: Compiling or linking the target; use BUILD_CODE.
Mutation-driven fuzzing as the primary operation; use FUZZ_TEST.
Explicit assessment of a proposed change; use VALIDATE_CHANGE.
include: Running a binary or script on supplied arguments or files.
Executing a target that emits diagnostics, traces, return codes, or other output.

action_categories.definition: Executes deliberate test cases, test inputs, corpus entries, or deterministic checks against a target.
exclude: Automatically mutating or generating inputs at scale; use FUZZ_TEST.
Validation of a proposed patch or change as the primary purpose; use VALIDATE_CHANGE.
include: Running selected inputs, replaying reproducer inputs, or probing boundary cases.
Executing sanitizer-backed tests or exhaustive checks.

action_categories.definition: Drives a target with automatically generated or mutated inputs, usually using seeds, a corpus, coverage feedback, or multiple workers.
exclude: Building the fuzz target; use BUILD_CODE.
Running one deliberately selected input; use RUN_TEST.
include: Launching fuzzing runs or structure-aware fuzzing.
Generating or mutating corpus entries while executing a fuzz target.

action_categories.definition: Applies an existing patch or diff to source files or a file set.
exclude: Creating a patch artifact; use GENERATE_PATCH.
Directly editing source without applying a patch; use MODIFY_FILE.
include: Applying a generated patch to a source tree.
Attempting patch application before rebuilding or testing.

action_categories.definition: Assesses a proposed patch, fix, reproducer, or other change against expected behavior or checks.
exclude: Creating or editing the change itself; use GENERATE_PATCH or MODIFY_FILE.
Generic testing not tied to a proposed change; use RUN_TEST.
include: Validating a reproducer with and without a change.
Applying, building, and testing a proposed change as an assessment.

message_roles.definition: States an intended investigation, experiment, construction, validation, or next action.
exclude: Reporting completed or current work without intent; use STATUS_UPDATE or RESULT_REPORT.
A causal explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Plans to inspect, build, test, trace, generate, or change something.
Conditional statements about what will be done next.

message_roles.definition: Reports the current state or progress of an ongoing activity or artifact.
exclude: A future plan; use INTENT_STATEMENT.
A causal explanation; use DIAGNOSIS.
A specific observed outcome presented as evidence; use RESULT_REPORT.
include: Describing work as in progress, completed, blocked, still under investigation, or awaiting a result.
Reporting current validation, build, or debugging status.

message_roles.definition: Explains implementation structure, data flow, call paths, or observed technical mechanisms.
exclude: An asserted cause of a defect; use DIAGNOSIS.
A proposed fix; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
include: Describing how a harness maps inputs to calls.
Tracing functions, APIs, buffers, source definitions, or execution paths.

message_roles.definition: States or revises an explanation for a defect, failure, or observed behavior.
exclude: A neutral implementation description; use TECHNICAL_ANALYSIS.
A proposed corrective action without causal explanation; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
include: Bug diagnoses, hypotheses, root-cause claims, and hypothesis revisions.
Explaining why an observed failure or memory-safety issue occurs.

message_roles.definition: Reports a discovered condition, bug, evidence, or confirmed technical observation.
exclude: A tentative explanation without an established observation; use DIAGNOSIS.
A test or validation outcome as the primary content; use RESULT_REPORT.
include: Reporting a newly found issue or confirmed behavior.
Summarizing evidence and identifying affected behavior or artifacts.

message_roles.definition: Proposes a fix, mitigation, or strategy for changing behavior or addressing a finding.
exclude: Reporting an already prepared or implemented fix; use REMEDIATION_UPDATE.
Reporting only the underlying cause; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Describing a planned patch or corrective code change.
Proposing a fallback, bounds check, validation rule, or other mitigation.

message_roles.definition: Reports an implemented, prepared, revised, or otherwise materialized fix or change.
exclude: A future fix proposal; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
A test result about the fix; use RESULT_REPORT.
include: Describing a completed source change or prepared patch artifact.
Reporting that a corrective implementation has been adjusted or is ready for assessment.

message_roles.definition: Reports observed outcomes from tests, builds, validation, experiments, or diagnostic runs without classifying them as successful or unsuccessful.
exclude: A plan to run the check; use INTENT_STATEMENT.
A causal explanation of the result; use DIAGNOSIS.
include: Reporting crashes, warnings, clean observations, errors, coverage changes, or validation results.
Summarizing what an executed check or experiment produced.

message_roles.definition: Reports a change in investigative, testing, comparison, or debugging method or focus.
exclude: A routine progress update without a change in method; use STATUS_UPDATE.
A proposed code fix; use REMEDIATION_PLAN.
include: Shifting from one hypothesis, source area, input strategy, or analysis method to another.
Explaining why the current approach is being redirected.

message_subjects.definition: Program structure, entry points, APIs, call paths, and source-level implementation details under examination.
exclude: Repository history or version metadata; use SOURCE_VARIANTS_AND_REPOSITORY.
Runtime diagnostic output without structural analysis; use SANITIZER_DIAGNOSTICS.
include: Harness wiring, function definitions, immediate callees, callbacks, and source references.
Tracing how data reaches a library or program component.

message_subjects.definition: Compilers, build scripts, build configuration, instrumentation settings, packaging, and build outputs.
exclude: Running an already built target; use VALIDATION_AND_TESTING or FUZZING_AND_CORPORA.
Source-level bug mechanism without build context; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW.
include: Compilation, sanitizer-enabled builds, amalgamation, build trees, and toolchain warnings.
Searching or comparing alternate built or packaged implementations.

message_subjects.definition: Source copies, implementation variants, repository history, version comparisons, and repository state.
exclude: A newly generated patch as the main subject; use PATCHING_AND_REMEDIATION.
General filesystem placement or artifact size; use FILESYSTEM_AND_ARTIFACTS.
include: Differential source analysis, historical fix lookup, repository metadata, and local packaging comparisons.
Comparing alternate implementations or revisions.

message_subjects.definition: Files, directories, paths, artifact placement, copying, presence, and simple artifact metadata.
exclude: The semantic contents of source or parser code; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW.
Patch logic as the main subject; use PATCHING_AND_REMEDIATION.
include: Source trees, output files, corpus directories, file paths, sizes, and artifact organization.
Problems involving missing, added, updated, or removed files.

message_subjects.definition: Corrective source changes, patch contents, patch formatting, patch paths, and fix artifacts.
exclude: The underlying defect mechanism without the corrective change; use MEMORY_SAFETY or PARSING_AND_DECODING.
Generic source comparison; use SOURCE_VARIANTS_AND_REPOSITORY.
include: Patch preparation, application, formatting, pathing, and targeted source fixes.
Discussion of how a proposed remediation changes behavior.

message_subjects.definition: Crafted, minimized, boundary, malformed, or fault-reproducing inputs used for analysis or testing.
exclude: Corpus management or mutation at scale; use FUZZING_AND_CORPORA.
The harness that consumes the input; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW.
include: Reproducer files, proof-of-concept inputs, compressed streams, parser fixtures, and boundary cases.
Designing or reducing inputs to expose a behavior.

message_subjects.definition: Fuzz targets, input mutation, seed generation, corpus management, and fuzzing diagnostics.
exclude: A single handcrafted input or reproducer; use TEST_INPUTS_AND_REPRODUCERS.
Building the target without fuzzing activity; use BUILD_AND_TOOLCHAIN.
include: Fuzzing runs, workers, corpus entries, reductions, coverage progress, and crash discovery.
Structure-aware or sanitizer-backed fuzzing.

message_subjects.definition: Deliberate tests, regression checks, replay, validation assessments, and their observed outcomes.
exclude: Automatic mutation-driven exploration; use FUZZING_AND_CORPORA.
The code defect mechanism itself; use MEMORY_SAFETY or PARSING_AND_DECODING.
include: Testing a change against a reproducer or test suite.
Running selected inputs, deterministic checks, or validation harnesses.

message_subjects.definition: Memory-safety instrumentation, sanitizer configurations, sanitizer reports, and diagnostic traces.
exclude: Ordinary tests without diagnostic instrumentation; use VALIDATION_AND_TESTING.
The underlying source-level memory defect; use MEMORY_SAFETY.
include: Address, memory, or similar sanitizer builds and reports.
Uninitialized-value, use-after-free, trace, and origin diagnostics.

message_subjects.definition: Memory-lifetime, initialization, bounds, allocation, and invalid-access behavior.
exclude: Only reporting sanitizer output without interpreting the defect; use SANITIZER_DIAGNOSTICS.
Non-memory functional conversion or lookup issues; use DATA_CONVERSION or TABLE_LOOKUP_VALIDATION.
include: Use-after-free, uninitialized reads, buffer overflows, invalid offsets, and unsafe copying.
Reasoning about memory-safety consequences of parser or data-structure logic.

message_subjects.definition: Parsing, decoding, decompression, encoded-format handling, and format-specific control flow.
exclude: Generic file access or path operations; use FILESYSTEM_AND_ARTIFACTS.
Memory-lifetime consequences as the main topic; use MEMORY_SAFETY or BUFFER_POINTER_AND_BOUNDS.
include: Chunk readers, compressed streams, decoder symbols, parse paths, and format metadata.
Investigating how malformed or unusual encoded data is processed.

message_subjects.definition: Pointer lifetime, buffer sizing, offset tracking, bounds checks, and overlapping or repeated-copy behavior.
exclude: General parser behavior without buffer or pointer focus; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
Linked-run or other abstract data-structure invariants; use DATA_STRUCTURE_INVARIANTS.
include: Stale pointers, output-buffer state, allocation sizing, backreference distances, and copy-loop boundaries.
Checking whether indices, lengths, or offsets are validated before use.

message_subjects.definition: Invariants and mutation rules for linked, indexed, or stateful data structures.
exclude: Raw buffer or pointer arithmetic; use BUFFER_POINTER_AND_BOUNDS.
Generic parser control flow; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
include: Run merging, link consistency, isolate boundaries, compaction, and structural bookkeeping.
Reasoning about whether mutations preserve relationships between elements.

message_subjects.definition: Generated or packed lookup tables and validation of values used to index them.
exclude: General source searching without table semantics; use SOURCE_STRUCTURE_AND_CALL_FLOW.
Numeric conversion without lookup indexing; use DATA_CONVERSION.
include: Table generation, lookup macros, code-point or symbol ranges, and upper-bound checks.
Investigating out-of-range input values reaching table access.

message_subjects.definition: Conversion, normalization, encoding, or decoding of values between representations.
exclude: Parsing the enclosing file format; use PARSING_AND_DECODING.
Table-index bounds as the primary issue; use TABLE_LOOKUP_VALIDATION.
include: Character-set, sample, pixel, bit-depth, gamma, or other representation conversions.
Checking conversion bounds and normalization behavior.

object_categories.definition: Textual content stored or handled as a file or bounded artifact.
exclude: Opaque encoded bytes; use BINARY_ARTIFACT.
Runnable compiled programs; use EXECUTABLE.
include: Source, headers, scripts, configuration, logs, patches, changelogs, and generated text.
Text excerpts or textual command output.

object_categories.definition: Opaque or encoded binary data stored as a file or stream.
exclude: Source or other text handled as text; use TEXT_ARTIFACT or SOURCE_CODE.
A runnable compiled program; use EXECUTABLE.
include: Images, compressed streams, raw crash data, and binary outputs.
Files inspected or generated as byte sequences.

object_categories.definition: Program source, headers, generated source, or a source variant.
exclude: Compiled or linked output; use BUILD_ARTIFACT or EXECUTABLE.
A patch representation rather than source contents; use PATCH.
include: Implementation files, declarations, macros, test drivers, and copied source variants.
Generated code used as program source.

object_categories.definition: A directory tree containing source code and related project files.
exclude: A standalone file; use SOURCE_CODE or TEXT_ARTIFACT.
A corpus or artifact collection; use FUZZ_CORPUS or DIRECTORY.
include: Source repositories, library trees, test trees, and build-input trees.

object_categories.definition: A filesystem directory or path container used to hold files or artifacts.
exclude: A collection defined by its fuzzing inputs; use FUZZ_CORPUS.
A file or stream; use TEXT_ARTIFACT or BINARY_ARTIFACT.
include: Build, output, corpus, temporary, source, and artifact directories.

object_categories.definition: Settings or parameters that control a build, test, validator, or tool.
exclude: Program source implementing behavior; use SOURCE_CODE.
Observed diagnostic output; use DIAGNOSTIC_OUTPUT.
include: Configuration files, build options, sanitizer settings, and command parameters.

object_categories.definition: A runnable binary, script, fuzzer, harness, or test program.
exclude: Uncompiled source; use SOURCE_CODE.
A non-runnable input file; use TEST_INPUT or BINARY_ARTIFACT.
include: Compiled test targets, command-line programs, scripts, and instrumented executables.

object_categories.definition: Output produced by a build or instrumentation process, including build trees and compiled artifacts.
exclude: Original source inputs; use SOURCE_CODE or SOURCE_TREE.
A deliberately supplied test input; use TEST_INPUT.
include: Compiled libraries, object files, instrumented outputs, and temporary build trees.
Build products that may contain one or more executables.

object_categories.definition: A source-level program component or implementation unit.
exclude: The complete runnable target; use EXECUTABLE.
A generated lookup-data artifact; use LOOKUP_TABLE.
include: Functions, APIs, callbacks, parsers, decoders, copy loops, and data-structure implementations.
Entry points and immediate callees examined during analysis.

object_categories.definition: A driver that converts inputs into calls to a program or library target.
exclude: The target implementation itself; use PROGRAM_COMPONENT.
The input supplied to the driver; use TEST_INPUT or FUZZ_CORPUS.
include: Fuzzer entrypoints, validator drivers, test harnesses, and input adapters.

object_categories.definition: A selected or generated input used to exercise a program or parser.
exclude: A collection of many fuzz inputs; use FUZZ_CORPUS.
Source code or a patch; use SOURCE_CODE or PATCH.
include: Handcrafted streams, encoded files, boundary cases, seed files, and test fixtures.
Inputs used for ordinary tests or exploratory probes.

object_categories.definition: A test input intended to reproduce a specific observed fault or abnormal behavior.
exclude: General-purpose seeds without a reproduction purpose; use TEST_INPUT or FUZZ_CORPUS.
The patch intended to address the fault; use PATCH.
include: Crash inputs, minimized reproducers, and proof-of-concept inputs.
Inputs retained for regression or patch validation.

object_categories.definition: A collection of seed, mutated, reduced, or otherwise retained fuzzing inputs.
exclude: A single deliberately crafted reproducer; use REPRODUCER_INPUT.
A directory with no corpus role; use DIRECTORY.
include: Fuzzing corpus directories and their individual retained entries.
Corpus snapshots used to seed or replay fuzzing.

object_categories.definition: A textual diff or patch representation of changes to files or source.
exclude: The modified source itself; use SOURCE_CODE.
A comparison that is not materialized as a patch; use SOURCE_CODE or TEXT_ARTIFACT.
include: Unified diffs, patch files, repository-style change headers, and fix artifacts.
A patch prepared for application or validation.

object_categories.definition: Generated, packed, or indexed table data used by program logic.
exclude: General source code not serving as table data; use SOURCE_CODE.
Runtime table state held during execution; use RUNTIME_STATE.
include: Generated character, symbol, macro, or lookup tables and their generators.
Table definitions and table-related artifacts examined for bounds issues.

object_categories.definition: Mutable execution state relevant to program behavior or diagnostics.
exclude: Static source definitions; use PROGRAM_COMPONENT or SOURCE_CODE.
A diagnostic report describing the state; use DIAGNOSTIC_OUTPUT.
include: Buffers, pointer state, allocator state, decoder state, copy offsets, and table state.
Callback or output state observed during tracing.

object_categories.definition: Output that records warnings, traces, sanitizer findings, coverage information, or other execution diagnostics.
exclude: The executable or input that produced the output; use EXECUTABLE or TEST_INPUT.
Source text being inspected; use TEXT_ARTIFACT.
include: Compiler warnings, sanitizer reports, trace logs, corpus-progress output, and error diagnostics.
Observed return codes or process messages when treated as evidence.

object_categories.definition: Version-control or repository information rather than the repository's file contents.
exclude: Source files and their text; use SOURCE_CODE or TEXT_ARTIFACT.
An independently generated patch artifact; use PATCH.
include: History, status, tags, repository identity, and repository-level differences.
